message.content:
Repo: ~/imsgct/imscribe.com (a Python/FastAPI-backed static site, deployed to fly.io). The directory ~/imsgct/imscribe.com/index/ holds ~25 standalone HTML pages, each largely self-contained (own inline <style>, sometimes own fonts/color palette). The main entry point is index/index.html — a long single-page "SOLVATUM" themed landing page (alchemical stages, achievements section, a "Cosmic Kernel Spotlight" card linking to k3vM.html, a crystal-of-types section, etc — dark background, gold/Cinzel-serif styling, CSS variables --bg/--gold/--text etc).

Task: catalog every HTML page under index/ (skip .bak files, skip index/anim, index/images, index/ovm subdirectories unless they hold pages — check if ovm/index.html is a real page). For each page report:
1. Filename
2. Page <title> and any masthead/heading text
3. One-sentence description of what it actually shows (read enough of the body/script to tell: is it a 3D visualization, a data table, a reference document, an interactive tool, a static essay?)
4. Its own color/font scheme if distinct from index.html's gold/Cinzel/dark theme described above (note if it reuses the same variables or has a totally different look)
5. Whether it is currently linked FROM index.html (grep index.html for the filename) and whether it links back TO index.html or anywhere else (grep the page for href to other .html files in this same index/ dir)
6. Its approximate file size / line count (already known for most, but confirm for any not listed: IG_OVERVIEW.html, IG_primitive_map_3d.html, epsilon_tilt.html, frobenius-mzi.html, geo_map.html, ig_genes.html, ig_pt_web.html, imasm.html, inquire.html, k3v-with-dialects.html, k3vM.html, magnum_opus_lattice.html, necessity.html, rune_gnosis.html, solar_seismic.html, voynich_callgraph_3d.html, voynich_cfg.html, voynich_phytoglyphica.html, ovm/index.html)

Also check: does web/api.py serve these via StaticFiles mount, and is there any existing nav/header component shared across pages (grep for a common <nav> or header pattern across a few pages)?

This is read-only research for a plan — do not edit anything. Report back a structured table (filename | title | one-line content description | distinct styling? | linked from index? | links back?) plus the api.py static-serving note. Keep the report focused and complete — I need every page accounted for, not a sample.

attachment.content:
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
## Findings

**Scope covered:** all 20 `.html` files directly under `index/` (excluding `.bak2/3/4/5`), plus `index/ovm/index.html` (a real page — a distinct OVM Viewer app). `index/anim` and `index/images` are asset dirs, not pages. `index/google7c0be3c906655308.html` is a 1-line Google site-verification stub (not a content page — content: `google-site-verification: google7c0be3c906655308.html`). There's also a stray `index/k3vM.html:Zone.Identifier` (Windows-download artifact, not an HTML page, harmless but could be cleaned up).

### Page catalog

| Filename | Title / heading | Content | Styling | Linked from index.html? | Links back? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **IG_OVERVIEW.html** (642 ln, 31KB) | "The Imscribing Grammar — Axiomatic Specification" | Long-form reference doc/spec (axioms/prose) | Reuses same palette: `--bg:#0a0a08 --gold:#b8922a --accent:#c4a35a`, IBM Plex Mono + IM Fell English (same family as index) | Yes | No |
| **IG_primitive_map_3d.html** (95 ln but 6.4MB, one giant line) | none (no `<title>`/`<h1>`) | Raw exported Plotly 3D scatter/graph (huge inlined data arrays), navy bg `#0F0F1A`, no chrome/nav at all | Totally different — bare Plotly export, no theme | Yes | No |
| **epsilon_tilt.html** (1260 ln, 75KB) | "The Universe Resolves Its Own Indecision — C. L. Mills" | Static essay/paper | Distinct gold variants (`--gold:#c8960a` etc.) but same gold-on-dark family, own var namespace | Yes | No |
| **frobenius-mzi.html** (887 ln, 37KB) | "Frobenius Mesh 3x3 \| Looping Photons • Complex MZI Matrix & SVD" (h2 "MZI MESH 3×3", "COMPLEX MATRIX A") | Interactive 3D visualization (THREE.js) of a photonic mesh + matrix/SVD panels | Totally different: Inter sans-serif, not gold/Cinzel | Yes | No |
| **geo_map.html** (994 ln, 49KB) | "Datanado — Geographic Signal Propagation" (h1 "🌍 DATANADO") | Interactive tool/map with `<canvas>` (signal propagation visualization) | Different: JetBrains Mono/Fira Code, own scheme | No (0 hits) | No |
| **ig_genes.html** (465 ln, 17KB) | "Paraconsistent Genetics — Animations · Imscribe" | Animated/illustrated essay | Reuses index vars (`--bg`, `--text`) + Cinzel/EB Garamond, close to index theme | Yes | **Yes** — has `<nav>` and `href="index.html"` |
| **ig_pt_web.html** (208 ln, 22KB) | "IG Periodic Table — 3D" | Interactive 3D visualization (THREE.js + OrbitControls) of a periodic-table-style structure; drag/scroll/hover controls | Different: system-ui sans-serif, minimal chrome | Yes | No |
| **imasm.html** (4063 ln, 262KB) | "IMASM · Live Horn Torus · Imscribing Grammar" (h1 "mOMonadOS Kernel — UCFm Geometry · agent_loop (1,1)") | Interactive 3D visualization (THREE.js) — live "horn torus" kernel geometry graph | Different: system-ui sans-serif | No (0 hits — note: index links to **k3vM.html**, not this one, per the "Cosmic Kernel Spotlight") | No |
| **inquire.html** (535 ln, 15KB) | "Oracle — Imscribing Grammar" | Interactive tool — an "Oracle" query/chat-style interface | Reuses index-like gold vars (`--bg:#0d0c0a --gold:#c8a850`), Cinzel | Yes | No |
| **k3v-with-dialects.html** (4418 ln, 289KB) | "mOMonadOS Kernel — agent_loop (1,1) on the horn torus · IMASM graph" | Interactive 3D visualization (THREE.js), variant of the kernel/horn-torus graph "with dialects" | Different: system-ui sans-serif | No (0 hits) | No |
| **k3vM.html** (4817 ln, 321KB) | same title as k3v-with-dialects | Interactive 3D visualization (THREE.js) — this is the one linked as the "Cosmic Kernel Spotlight" card | Different: system-ui sans-serif | **Yes** (2 hits) | No |
| **magnum_opus_lattice.html** (843 ln, 85KB) | "Belnap FOUR as unit square — alchemical palette" (sr-only h2 describes it as a Belnap bilattice / Standard-Model gauge-hierarchy explorer) | Interactive tool/diagram — logic-lattice explorer in "alchemical" styling | Distinct gold var set (`--gold:#c8960a` etc.), close cousin of index theme but separate namespace | Yes | No |
| **necessity.html** (659 ln, 30KB) | "The Necessity of the Grammar" | Static essay/argument | Reuses exact index vars (`--bg:#0a0a08 --gold:#b8922a --accent:#c4a35a`), same fonts | Yes | No |
| **rune_gnosis.html** (171 ln, 9KB) | no `<title>`; h-title "The Rune Gnosis" ("Canto I · Vinit") | Static poetic/mythic essay (runic verse) | Distinct look: IM Fell English + Cinzel, own gold tones, Norse rune glyphs — thematically different content but same gold-on-dark family | Yes | No |
| **solar_seismic.html** (616 ln, 31KB) | "Solar–Seismic Coupling Map" (h1 "⚡ SEISMIC COUPLING OBSERVATORY") | Data visualization/dashboard | Different: JetBrains Mono | Yes | No |
| **voynich_callgraph_3d.html** (63 ln but 152KB, long lines) | none (`<title>`/`<h1>` absent) | Raw exported Plotly 3D graph (call-graph style, div id `voynich-graph`), plain bg, no chrome | Totally different — bare Plotly export | Yes | No |
| **voynich_cfg.html** (1004 ln, 37KB) | "Voynich Engine — Plant Session CFG" (h1 "Voynich Phytoglyphica") | Reference/diagram document (control-flow-graph style) for the Voynich plant material | Reuses index-like gold vars (`--bg:#0d0c0a --gold:#c8a850`) | Yes | **Yes** — `href="index.html"` present |
| **voynich_phytoglyphica.html** (2761 ln, 291KB) | "Voynich Phytoglyphica — Annotated Folios · imscribe.com" | Reference document — annotated manuscript folios | Totally different: Noto Sans Shavian / Unifont / Code2001 (constructed-script fonts), not gold/Cinzel | Yes | No |
| **ovm/index.html** (859 ln, 44KB) | "OVM Viewer — Operator-Valued Measure Visualization" | Interactive 3D visualization (THREE.js) — a standalone app, real page (not a placeholder) | Totally different: Georgia/Times New Roman serif | Yes (index links to `ovm/` directory, line 1853, as a "repo-card" `target="_blank"`) | No |

### Additional non-page files
- `google7c0be3c906655308.html` — Google site-verification stub, 1 line, not a real page.
- `k3vM.html:Zone.Identifier` — stray Windows Alternate-Data-Stream artifact from a downloaded file; not an HTML page, safe to ignore/delete later.

### Shared nav / header
No shared nav/header component exists across pages — every page is fully standalone with its own inline `<style>`. Only **two** pages (`ig_genes.html`, `voynich_cfg.html`) contain any `<nav>`/link back to `index.html`; all others are dead-ends with no way back to the landing page once you click through from `index.html`.

### `web/api.py` static serving (important finding)
```
web/api.py:228  _INDEX_DIR = _ROOT / "index"
web/api.py:246  _REQUIRED = [_INDEX_DIR, _INDEX_DIR / "inquire.html"]
web/api.py:255-256  StaticFiles mounted at /static -> index/
web/api.py:257-258  StaticFiles mounted at /images  -> index/images/
web/api.py:277-279  @app.get("/") returns FileResponse(index/inquire.html)
```
**Notable:** the FastAPI root route `"/"` serves `inquire.html`, not `index.html`. `index.html` (the big SOLVATUM landing page) is only reachable via the `/static/` mount (e.g. `/static/index.html`), not at the site root. All other pages cataloged above are likewise only reachable via `/static/<filename>.html` (or `/static/ovm/`) — there is no dedicated FastAPI route per page, it's a flat static mount over the whole `index/` directory.
